title: Proof Protocol
concept: Real change is a behavior, plus evidence you can both see, plus a set time window. A promise with none of those is just hope.
whenToUse: After any real request for change; whenever “I promise” shows up with no actual plan; instead of just hoping things get better.
steps: Name the change — be specific and something you can actually observe.
Decide what counts — what does met, partial, and missed look like?
Set a time window — start date, end date, and when you'll check in.
Track it simply — a tally or a table. Look at the facts first when you check in.
Check in — extend it, adjust it, or close it out. Stay on the same team.
If it keeps getting missed without anyone owning it, that's worth raising.

phrases.text: I need proof, not a promise. The change: ___. Evidence: ___. Window: ___. Check-in: ___.
I’m committing to ___, visible as ___, through ___.
At check-in, let's look at the record first.

working: Pause + Return always comes with an exact time; tracked for 14 days; six times out of six kept → trust moves forward.
notWorking: “I’ll be better at communicating.” No specific behavior, no evidence, no time window. It feels good for a minute and changes nothing.
activity: Write one proof item today: the behavior, the evidence, the time window, and when you'll check in. Both of you sign off on it.
